page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8163 processor cores running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 8.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the processor performance is generally modest. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench place the instance in the bottom 25% and bottom 10% tiers respectively. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in large-block uncached memory read and write operations, as well as in Passmark CPU physics and extended instruction tests. Redis SET operations also achieve average throughput at 5.94 million operations per second, though database operations and cached memory bandwidth remain in the lower 25% tier.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1.2xlarge is its lower compute performance relative to its high memory capacity. While the 64.0 GB RAM allocation provides high resource density for memory-bound tasks, the older Intel Xeon 8163 architecture limits its suitability for compute-heavy workloads like large-scale LLM inference or intensive software compilation. Qualitatively, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-frequency CPU performance or local NVMe storage, such as caching layers, Redis deployments, and moderate database operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, though it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate modest compute capabilities, with single-core and multi-core CPU metrics falling into the lower 25% tier. However, the instance maintains average throughput for uncached large-block memory operations and Redis SET benchmarks. Lacking local NVMe storage and high-speed network baselines, the ecs.se1.2xlarge is best suited for memory-intensive workloads with moderate CPU demands, such as distributed caching, in-memory databases, and lightweight backend services.
